source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-16

procedures.title: Delcotron brushes: replace (6.2" Delcotron)
steps: Check the brushes; replace them if worn halfway.
Check the brush springs for distortion or weakness; reuse them if the brushes look good and slide freely in the holder.
Push the brushes into the holder and insert the pin to hold them there.
Fasten the brush assembly and condenser to the end frame with the hex-head stud on the left side only.
Route the leads as in figure 18c of the manual, with the right-hand brush lead under the right-hand hex-head stud.
Fit the terminal cover with 2 screws, keeping all leads out from under it.

procedures.title: Double contact voltage regulator: remove and install
steps: Disconnect the battery ground cable and the harness connector at the regulator.
Remove the screws holding the regulator to the car.
After any mechanical adjustment, check and adjust the electrical settings.
Before fitting the cover, make sure the rubber gasket is in place on the regulator base.
notes: Most adjustments are made on the car; remove the regulator only for field relay point and air gap work.
Never clean the voltage regulating contacts; their special material is ruined by any abrasive. Sooty or discolored contacts are normal after short use.

procedures.title: Field relay: mechanical adjustment
steps: Point opening: check as in figure 19c of the manual; if needed, carefully bend the armature stop.
Air gap: check with the points just touching (see figure 20c in the manual); it normally needs no adjustment.
notes: A feeler gauge gives only an approximate voltage regulator air gap setting.
